samples.claim: resolve_case_insensitive uses the same parser/error-to-None policy as resolve. For a single root or the first segment it prefers exact name, then first ASCII-case-insensitive match. Remaining segments use Field::resolve_case_insensitive. Ambiguous folded names use first match rather than error; original case is preserved in returned references. Unicode case folding is not used.
samples.review_note: Matches exact-first then first ASCII-folded root lookup, recursive resolution and original references; supplementary resolve230-242 confirms same parser/error-to-None.

samples.claim: MemWalIndexDetails centralizes configuration, base compaction progress, and shard snapshots. Writers read configuration; snapshots are point-in-time optimizations, while readers requiring current shards list directories and latest shard manifests. Background refresh does not make snapshots authoritative mutable shard state. Snapshot Lance-file schema lists shard_id utf8, shard_spec_id uint32, typed shard_field_{id}. snapshot_ts_millis int64=1 and num_shards uint32=2 describe it; optional inline_snapshots bytes=3 holds Lance bytes for small counts. The threshold example 100 is explicitly implementation-defined, not a specified constant.
samples.evidence:
636 | /* Index details for MemWAL Index, stored in IndexMetadata.index_details.
637 |  * This is the centralized structure for all MemWAL metadata:
638 |  * - Configuration (sharding specs, indexes to maintain)
639 |  * - SSTable compaction progress
640 |  * - Shard state snapshots
641 |  *
642 |  * Writers read this index to get configuration before writing.
643 |  * Readers may use shard snapshots in this index as a point-in-time
644 |  * optimization. Readers that need the latest shard set should list shard
645 |  * directories in storage and read each shard's latest manifest.
646 |  * A background process updates the index periodically to keep shard snapshots current.
647 |  *
648 |  * Shard snapshots are stored as a Lance file with one row per shard.
649 |  * The schema records shard discovery fields. Full mutable shard state remains
650 |  * authoritative in the shard manifest files.
651 |  *   shard_id: utf8
652 |  *   shard_spec_id: uint32
653 |  *   shard_field_{field_id}: typed per the matching ShardingField.result_type
654 |  */
655 | message MemWalIndexDetails {
656 |   // Snapshot timestamp (Unix timestamp in milliseconds).
657 |   int64 snapshot_ts_millis = 1;
658 | 
659 |   /* Number of shards in the snapshot.
660 |    * Used to determine storage format without reading the snapshot data.
661 |    */
662 |   uint32 num_shards = 2;
663 | 
664 |   /* Inline shard snapshots for small shard counts.
665 |    * When num_shards <= threshold (implementation-defined, e.g., 100),
666 |    * snapshots are stored inline as serialized bytes.
667 |    * Format: Lance file bytes with the shard snapshot schema.
668 |    */
669 |   optional bytes inline_snapshots = 3;
670 |

samples.claim: stress_shared_stream repeats 100 times with bounded capacity 2, two spawned consumers and 1000 sent integers. Each consumer asserts consecutive values as received and the test joins both. It does not separately assert the final counters equal 1000, so an early EOF could evade the per-item order check; actual timeout/duration and robustness were not measured.

samples.claim: pub(crate) project_by_ids recursively selects children, then returns the complete clone when the field id is selected and either no children were separately selected or include_all_children=true. If any child survives otherwise, it returns a trimmed clone; else None. Thus include_all_children=false plus parent-only selection still retains the whole subtree, while parent plus a selected child can trim it. IDs are tested with slice contains per node, not a bitmap; names and atomic blob/map semantics are not considered in this method.
samples.review_note: Matches child-first recursive selection and full-clone/trim/None branches, including parent-only false behavior.

samples.claim: pop examines the last block; an empty block is removed and pop recursively retries. A nonempty block decrements len and pops one value; no block means None. Removing a last value does not immediately remove its now-empty block. Ordering is LIFO across blocks and within each Vec. Repeated empty blocks cost recursive retries.
samples.review_note: Matches recursive empty-block removal, LIFO pop and deferred block deletion after last element.

samples.claim: MinHashLshIndexDetails is explicitly experimental: incompatible detail/file changes may require rebuilding the index, not rewriting data, and the feature may be removed if stabilization fails. Every segment must share identical details, query signatures must be comparable, and both index files repeat serialized details in schema metadata to detect mismatches. Readers validate every field before allocation or file read. num_hashes=1 is in [1,4096] and divisible by num_bands; num_bands=2 is in [1,256]; each band covers num_hashes/num_bands consecutive values.
